message.content:
**The three “great” schisms that most historians cite as the major ruptures in Christian history are:** | # | Schism | Approximate dates | Key causes & consequences | |---|--------|-------------------|---------------------------| | 1 | **The Great Schism (East‑West Schism)** | 1054 CE | • Long‑standing theological, liturgical, and political differences between the Byzantine (Eastern) and Latin (Western) churches.
• Disputes over the *Filioque* clause, the authority of the Pope, and differing rites.
• Formalized in 1054 when the Patriarch of Constantinople and the Papal legate excommunicated each other.
• Resulted in the permanent split between the Roman Catholic Church and the Eastern Orthodox Churches. | | 2 | **The Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | • Martin Luther’s 95 Theses (1517) sparked a wave of criticism of Catholic doctrine, practice, and corruption.
• Key issues: indulgences, papal authority, justification by faith, and the nature of the sacraments.
• Led to the creation of numerous Protestant denominations (Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican, Anabaptist, etc.).
• Triggered the Counter‑Reformation, the Council of Trent, and a series of religious wars across Europe. | | 3 | **The Old Catholic Schism (post‑First Vatican Council)** | 1870 CE onward | • The First Vatican Council (1869‑1870) defined papal infallibility and the *universal* nature of the Pope’s authority.
• A group of bishops and clergy in several European countries rejected these doctrines, arguing for a more conciliar and less centralized church structure.
• They formed the Old Catholic Church, which remains in communion with some other churches but is not part of the Roman Catholic hierarchy.
• This schism is often cited as the third major rupture because it challenged the very core of Catholic ecclesiology in the modern era. | ### Why these three are singled out 1. **Scale & longevity** – Each split involved entire national or continental churches and has persisted to the present day. 2. **Theological depth** – They addressed fundamental questions about authority, doctrine, and the nature of the church. 3. **Historical impact** – All three reshaped politics, culture, and the religious landscape of Europe and beyond. --- #### Quick reference | Schism | Year | Main split | |--------|------|------------| | Great Schism | 1054 | Roman Catholic ↔ Eastern Orthodox | | Protestant Reformation | 1517–1648 | Roman Catholic ↔ Protestant denominations | | Old Catholic Schism | 1870 | Roman Catholic ↔ Old Catholic Church | These are the three events most commonly referred to as the “great schisms” in Christian history.
